morningSummary: Good morning. Thursday, 12 November 2026. Today's international agenda is shaped by renewed military attacks involving Russia and Ukraine, alongside fresh diplomatic efforts following discussions in Abu Dhabi. In Nigeria, the African Democratic Congress leadership dispute remains unresolved as INEC awaits the certified court judgment. Kenya has discharged its last known Ebola patient and begun the 42-day countdown towards a possible declaration that the country is free of the outbreak. France faces questions about its 2027 political succession and a weaker economic outlook. In the United States, the results of the midterm elections have changed the political balance in Congress, raising important questions about accountability, executive power and the legislative agenda. G7 foreign ministers have reaffirmed support for Ukraine and discussed international security, while South Sudan faces concerns about its December election preparations. China and ASEAN have also missed their target for completing a South China Sea code of conduct. RadiantWaves Media brings you the facts, context and implications behind these developments.

featured.title: Ukraine war: attacks continue as diplomatic efforts intensify
featured.subtitle: US representatives are expected to meet Vladimir Putin after Abu Dhabi talks produced an agreement to arrange a prisoner exchange but no breakthrough on territorial disputes.
featured.description: Russia and Ukraine exchanged attacks on their respective capitals as Washington pursued another round of diplomatic engagement.
featured.content: Russia and Ukraine exchanged attacks early on Thursday, 12 November, underlining the continuing military dimension of the war despite renewed diplomatic activity. Explosions were heard in Kyiv, although the extent of any damage was not immediately established. Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin said five drones heading towards the Russian capital had been brought down. The latest developments followed two days of US-mediated discussions in Abu Dhabi. Russian and Ukrainian negotiators agreed to arrange a prisoner exchange, but the talks did not resolve the central disagreements over territory. US representatives Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff were expected to travel to Moscow to meet President Vladimir Putin. Their diplomatic mission also involves further engagement with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy and European leaders. The prisoner-exchange agreement is a humanitarian development, but it must not be confused with a ceasefire or a peace agreement. Fighting continues, and the fundamental disagreements over territory, sovereignty and security remain unresolved.
featured.whyItMatters: The conflict has consequences for European security, international diplomacy, energy markets, food supply chains and the future security arrangements of the continent.
featured.whatHappensNext: Attention will focus on the planned Moscow meeting, subsequent discussions with Ukraine and European leaders, and whether the agreed prisoner exchange can be implemented.

articles.title: Russia and Ukraine exchange attacks as US envoys prepare for Putin meeting
articles.summary: Fresh attacks on Kyiv and Moscow coincide with diplomatic efforts following discussions in Abu Dhabi.
articles.content: Russia and Ukraine exchanged attacks on their capitals early Thursday. Explosions were heard in Kyiv, although the full extent of damage was not immediately known. Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin said five drones heading towards Moscow had been intercepted. The latest military developments came after two days of US-mediated discussions in Abu Dhabi. Negotiators agreed to arrange a prisoner exchange, but no breakthrough was reported on the central dispute over territory. US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff were expected to meet Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow. The discussions are expected to address the diplomatic process and the possible involvement of European partners. Ukraine continues to insist that any sustainable settlement must protect its sovereignty and security. Russia's territorial demands remain a major obstacle. The agreement to arrange a prisoner exchange is significant for families affected by the war, but it does not constitute a ceasefire or a peace settlement.
articles.background: The war began with Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022. The conflict has caused extensive destruction, displacement and international security concerns.
articles.whyItMatters: Any settlement will affect Ukraine's territorial integrity, European defence policy, relations between Russia and Western governments and the wider international order.
articles.whatHappensNext: The planned Moscow meeting, further contacts with Zelenskyy and European leaders, and implementation of the prisoner-exchange agreement will be important developments to monitor.

articles.title: Nigeria's ADC leadership dispute remains unresolved as INEC awaits certified judgment
articles.summary: INEC Chairman Joash Amupitan says the commission needs the certified true copy of the Federal High Court judgment before determining its next steps.
articles.content: The dispute over the leadership of the African Democratic Congress remains an important development in Nigeria's opposition politics ahead of the 2027 general election. INEC Chairman Joash Amupitan has said that the commission needs the certified true copy of the Federal High Court judgment before it can properly consider the matter. The commission has indicated that it will not base an institutional decision solely on reports circulating on social media. The ruling delivered on 5 November challenged the position of the David Mark-led ADC leadership and decisions taken under that leadership. The development has implications for party administration and the political plans of opposition figures, including former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar. The ADC has indicated that it is pursuing legal remedies. It is important to distinguish between filing an appeal or an application for a stay and obtaining an actual court order suspending the effect of a judgment. Filing an appeal does not automatically suspend a court ruling. No confirmed stay order is established in the information reviewed for this report. The next steps will depend on the certified judgment, subsequent court proceedings and INEC's formal assessment.
articles.background: The ADC has become an important platform in discussions about opposition cooperation and political realignment ahead of the 2027 election.
articles.whyItMatters: The dispute could affect the party's recognised leadership, internal organisation and the political plans of aspirants seeking to contest under its platform.
articles.whatHappensNext: The key issues are delivery of the certified judgment to INEC, further court proceedings and any formal decision by the electoral commission.
articles.source: Premium Times; INEC statements; Federal High Court proceedings

articles.title: Kenya begins 42-day Ebola-free countdown after final patient is discharged
articles.summary: Kenya has discharged its last known Ebola patient and completed monitoring of the final identified contacts.
articles.content: Kenya reached an important milestone in its Ebola response after the country's last known patient was discharged on 11 November. The final 11 contacts also completed their monitoring on the same day. According to the World Health Organization's Regional Office for Africa, the 42-day countdown begins on 12 November. If no new cases are identified during this period, Kenya could be declared free of the outbreak on 23 December 2026. The outbreak involved nine confirmed cases, including two deaths, while seven people recovered. Health authorities identified and monitored 135 contacts. The cases were linked to the initial patient, and the WHO reported that there had been no community transmission. The countdown is an important milestone, but it does not mean surveillance can stop. Health teams must continue monitoring, investigating suspected cases and maintaining the ability to respond quickly.
articles.background: Kenya's outbreak involved the Bundibugyo strain of Ebola virus disease. The initial case was linked to travel from the Democratic Republic of the Congo through Uganda.
articles.whyItMatters: The response demonstrates the importance of contact tracing, early detection, public communication and cooperation between health authorities.
articles.whatHappensNext: Kenya must complete the 42-day monitoring period without another case before it can be declared free of the outbreak.
articles.source: World Health Organization Regional Office for Africa

articles.title: DR Congo continues Ebola response as regional health authorities maintain vigilance
articles.summary: The Democratic Republic of the Congo continues to face a major Ebola burden, with neighbouring countries monitoring the risk of further spread.
articles.content: The Democratic Republic of the Congo remains at the centre of a serious Ebola response. The European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control reported 11,042 confirmed cases and 5,387 related deaths in the DRC using data available up to 9 November. The outbreak has affected several provinces, and health authorities continue surveillance and response operations. The regional picture requires careful interpretation. Kenya's final patient has been discharged, while Nigeria's reported case involved a traveller with a history connected to Uganda who was medically evacuated to Switzerland. Nigerian authorities identified contacts and continued monitoring. This should not be presented as evidence of a sustained nationwide Ebola outbreak in Nigeria. The response depends on early diagnosis, safe treatment, contact tracing, infection prevention and accurate public communication.
articles.background: The current regional outbreak involves the Bundibugyo strain of Ebola virus. Several countries have strengthened surveillance and cross-border health coordination.
articles.whyItMatters: Cross-border health risks require cooperation between governments, airports, health agencies and international organisations. Accurate reporting helps prevent both complacency and unnecessary public panic.
articles.whatHappensNext: Authorities will continue monitoring suspected cases, contacts and cross-border risks. Updated figures from national health ministries and the WHO remain essential.
articles.source: European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control; WHO Africa

articles.title: Macron's public comments on Teddy Riner fuel France's 2027 succession debate
articles.summary: The French president's public reaction to judoka Teddy Riner's presidential announcement has attracted attention ahead of the 2027 election.
articles.content: France's political debate ahead of the 2027 presidential election has taken an unexpected turn following judoka Teddy Riner's announcement that he intends to run for president. President Emmanuel Macron publicly welcomed Riner's entry into the political debate. The comments have attracted attention because Macron cannot seek a third consecutive presidential term. Riner's announcement raises questions about whether a prominent figure from outside traditional party politics can build a credible national campaign. Public recognition and sporting achievements do not automatically translate into electoral support. A serious presidential campaign requires a detailed programme, political organisation, alliances and the ability to meet the legal requirements for candidacy. Macron's comments should not be interpreted as proof that he has organised or formally endorsed Riner's campaign.
articles.background: France will elect a new president in 2027. Macron is constitutionally unable to seek a third consecutive term, making political succession a major issue.
articles.whyItMatters: The development adds another potential figure to an already complex political landscape and may influence the positioning of established parties and candidates.
articles.whatHappensNext: Attention will focus on Riner's programme, campaign organisation, political alliances and whether the announcement develops into a fully established candidacy.

articles.title: Moody's lowers France's 2026 growth forecast to 0.2%
articles.summary: The reduced forecast adds pressure to France's economic and budgetary debate amid political uncertainty and high public debt.
articles.content: France's economic outlook has weakened after Moody's reduced its forecast for economic growth in 2026 to 0.2%. The revised projection is below the government's target of 0.5% and the Bank of France's forecast of 0.3%. Political uncertainty, difficult budget negotiations, borrowing costs and the country's public-finance position are among the concerns affecting the outlook. The revised forecast does not mean that France has entered a recession, but it signals a weaker growth environment. Slower growth can affect tax revenues, public spending plans, business confidence and employment. The challenge for the government is to manage public finances while supporting economic activity and maintaining confidence among investors and households.
articles.background: France has faced difficult negotiations over public spending, taxation and debt management. The country's economic performance is closely linked to wider conditions across the euro area.
articles.whyItMatters: A weaker growth outlook can complicate efforts to reduce public deficits and may influence borrowing costs, investment and household confidence.
articles.whatHappensNext: The next indicators to watch include economic growth figures, budget negotiations, government policy decisions and further assessments from rating agencies.

articles.title: French advisory body calls for stronger safeguards around artificial-intelligence assistants
articles.summary: A French advisory body has recommended stronger protections for users of AI assistants rather than an outright ban.
articles.content: France's Council on AI and Digital Technology has recommended stronger safeguards around artificial-intelligence assistants. The advice highlights risks including excessive dependence, misleading human-like interaction, emotional manipulation, hyper-personalisation and the vulnerability of younger users. The recommendations include stronger protections for minors, clearer disclosures, improved reporting mechanisms and greater transparency around advertising. The report does not call for a general ban on AI assistants. Instead, it argues that the technology should develop within a framework that protects users and makes companies more accountable. The debate reflects wider European questions about how to encourage innovation while addressing risks to privacy, wellbeing and public trust.
articles.background: AI assistants are increasingly used for education, work, information and personal communication. Governments and regulators are examining how existing rules should apply to these systems.
articles.whyItMatters: The debate could influence future regulation, product design and the responsibilities of companies providing AI services in France and across Europe.
articles.whatHappensNext: Attention will turn to how the recommendations are considered by policymakers and whether they lead to formal regulatory proposals.
articles.source: French Council on AI and Digital Technology; Le Monde

articles.title: G7 foreign ministers reaffirm support for Ukraine and maritime security
articles.summary: Ministers from Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan, the United Kingdom and the United States met in Paris on 9 and 10 November.
articles.content: G7 foreign ministers have reaffirmed their support for Ukraine following a meeting in Paris held under the French presidency of the group. The joint declaration, published on 11 November, addressed Ukraine, maritime security, Iran and other international challenges. The ministers condemned attacks affecting civilian shipping in the Black Sea and highlighted the consequences for global food security. They reiterated support for US-led diplomatic efforts while stressing that Europeans must be involved in negotiations concerning the future security of Europe. The statement also addressed Ukraine's financing needs for 2027 and beyond, air defence, energy resilience and sanctions against Russia. The meeting included Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan, the United Kingdom and the United States, together with the European Union's High Representative. The declaration is a statement of the participating governments' positions; it is not itself a ceasefire agreement or a settlement of the war.
articles.background: The G7 is a forum for major advanced economies to coordinate positions on economic, diplomatic and security matters.
articles.whyItMatters: The statement demonstrates continued coordination among major Western economies on Ukraine, maritime trade routes, energy security and international stability.
articles.whatHappensNext: The important test will be whether the commitments translate into financial support, practical security assistance and coordinated diplomatic action.
articles.source: GOV.UK; French Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs

articles.title: South Sudan warned over risks surrounding December election
articles.summary: An African Union envoy has warned that inadequate preparation and political tensions could threaten the planned 22 December election.
articles.content: South Sudan is facing renewed concern over preparations for its planned 22 December election. African Union envoy Jakaya Kikwete has urged international partners to help ensure that the electoral process is peaceful. Concerns include security, logistics, financing, political participation and the implementation of the country's peace arrangements. The political environment remains tense, with President Salva Kiir's government facing criticism over the slow implementation of transitional commitments. Opposition leader Riek Machar remains a central figure in the country's political crisis and is facing legal proceedings. The United Nations Mission in South Sudan has also highlighted concerns about the compressed timetable and the practical requirements for conducting an election. A vote held without sufficient preparation or political confidence could deepen instability rather than resolve it.
articles.background: South Sudan has experienced prolonged political and security instability since independence in 2011. The country's peace agreement has faced repeated implementation difficulties.
articles.whyItMatters: The election could influence the country's political legitimacy, security and humanitarian situation. A credible process is important for the country's long-term stability.
articles.whatHappensNext: The key issues are whether the authorities can provide adequate security, financing, logistics and meaningful political participation before the planned election date.

articles.title: China and ASEAN miss target for South China Sea code of conduct
articles.summary: Negotiators have made progress on the draft text but have not resolved disagreements needed to complete the agreement by the end of 2026.
articles.content: China and the Association of Southeast Asian Nations have missed their target for completing a code of conduct intended to manage tensions in the South China Sea. Reports indicate that around 80 per cent of the draft text has been provisionally agreed, but important questions remain unresolved. These include the geographic scope of the agreement, the meaning of sensitive legal provisions and whether the final document should be legally binding. The South China Sea is an important international shipping route and a source of overlapping territorial and maritime claims. Several Southeast Asian countries have disputes with China over maritime rights and activities. The failure to meet the deadline does not mean negotiations have ended. Discussions are expected to continue into 2027 under Singapore's ASEAN leadership.
articles.background: The South China Sea is strategically important for international trade, fishing, energy resources and regional security.
articles.whyItMatters: Unresolved maritime disputes can increase the risk of confrontation and affect shipping, trade and relations between China and neighbouring countries.
articles.whatHappensNext: Negotiators will continue discussions on the unresolved legal and geographic questions as ASEAN prepares for the next phase of negotiations.

articles.title: Trinidad and Tobago Privy Council ruling raises major human-rights questions
articles.summary: The Judicial Committee of the Privy Council has issued a decision in the challenge to provisions criminalising consensual same-sex intimacy between adults.
articles.content: The Judicial Committee of the Privy Council has delivered a judgment in the case of Jason Jones v Attorney General of Trinidad and Tobago, reported as [2026] UKPC 38. The case concerns provisions of the Sexual Offences Act that criminalise certain consensual same-sex activity between adults in private. The Privy Council allowed the appeal and dismissed the cross-appeal. The court's decision addresses the legal challenge, but the final remedial order is to follow further submissions. It is therefore important not to report that every relevant provision has already been fully removed from the statute without explaining the outstanding remedial stage. The case has implications for constitutional rights, privacy, equality and the relationship between national law and the Privy Council's appellate jurisdiction.
articles.background: The Privy Council is the final court of appeal for Trinidad and Tobago. The case concerns the interpretation and constitutional validity of provisions of the country's Sexual Offences Act.
articles.whyItMatters: The judgment is significant for human-rights protections and the legal treatment of consensual private relationships between adults.
articles.whatHappensNext: Further submissions are required before the final remedial order. The precise legal effect should be assessed against that order when issued.
articles.source: Judicial Committee of the Privy Council; [2026] UKPC 38

articles.title: US midterm results reshape Congress and open a new accountability debate
articles.summary: Democratic gains in the 2026 midterm elections have changed the balance of power in Congress, setting up a period of oversight and political confrontation.
articles.content: The 2026 US midterm elections have reshaped the political balance in Washington. Associated Press reporting says Democrats' victories have given the party majorities in both chambers of Congress. The result creates the prospect of more intensive congressional scrutiny of the Trump administration during the remaining two years of the president's term. Incoming House Oversight chair Robert Garcia has indicated that investigations into the administration will be a priority. President Donald Trump and Attorney General Todd Blanche have criticised the prospect of extensive investigations, warning that Democratic demands could become politically motivated. Democratic leaders face their own challenge: demonstrating that congressional oversight will address matters of public interest rather than become a substitute for a policy programme. The election result is a political mandate, but it does not automatically resolve disagreements over the economy, immigration, government spending, judicial appointments or executive authority. The effectiveness of the new Congress will depend on its ability to scrutinise government conduct, legislate and respond to voters' concerns.
articles.background: Midterm elections determine the composition of Congress and can significantly change the relationship between the executive and legislative branches of government.
articles.whyItMatters: Congress has constitutional responsibilities to legislate, oversee federal agencies and scrutinise the executive branch. The new political balance will influence investigations, budgets and national policy.
articles.whatHappensNext: Attention will turn to the transition of congressional leadership, committee priorities, proposed investigations and the ability of both parties to agree on legislation.

editorial.title: Democracy requires more than political announcements
editorial.description: Democracy is not measured by speeches, campaign promises or announcements alone. It depends on institutions that can function independently, laws that apply equally, credible elections, accountable leadership and citizens who can question those in power without fear.
editorial.content: Across the world, political leaders regularly speak about defending democracy. Yet democratic credibility is built through conduct, not slogans. Elections must be credible, courts must be able to make decisions independently, public institutions must be accountable and citizens must have meaningful opportunities to participate. The United States midterm elections, Nigeria's ongoing party leadership dispute and political tensions in several other countries demonstrate why democratic institutions matter. A party's political ambitions cannot replace legal procedures. An election victory does not remove the responsibility to govern fairly. Opposition parties also have a duty to respect democratic rules, internal accountability and transparency. Democracy is strongest when those who win power accept scrutiny and those who lose elections can trust the process.
editorial.whyItMatters: Public trust depends on whether democratic principles are reflected in institutional behaviour and everyday governance.

analysis.title: The gap between diplomacy and reality in the Ukraine war
analysis.description: A prisoner-exchange agreement is a humanitarian step, but it should not be mistaken for progress on the central territorial and security disputes.
analysis.content: Diplomatic meetings can create opportunities for communication, but their importance must be measured by what they actually deliver. The Abu Dhabi discussions produced an agreement to arrange a prisoner exchange, an important humanitarian development. However, the central disagreements over territory and Ukraine's future security remain unresolved. The continuation of attacks during diplomatic engagement demonstrates the distance between negotiation and conditions on the ground. European participation will also remain a major question because any settlement affecting European security cannot realistically be treated as a matter involving only Washington, Moscow and Kyiv.
analysis.whyItMatters: International audiences need to distinguish humanitarian progress from a political settlement or ceasefire.

analysis.title: Nigeria's opposition needs clarity as the 2027 political season approaches
analysis.description: The ADC leadership dispute highlights the importance of clear party structures, transparent legal processes and credible opposition organisation.
analysis.content: The ADC dispute is not simply a disagreement between political personalities. It raises questions about party leadership, institutional recognition and the legal procedures through which political organisations operate. For opposition figures seeking to challenge the governing party in 2027, clarity and stability will be essential. INEC must act within the law and rely on the relevant court documents. Party leaders and supporters should avoid presenting applications, appeals or political declarations as final legal outcomes. The credibility of the opposition will depend not only on its criticism of government but also on its ability to demonstrate internal organisation, transparency and respect for due process.
analysis.whyItMatters: Opposition credibility and electoral competition are important elements of democratic accountability.

factCheck.title: Fact Check: Has the Russia–Ukraine war ended following the Abu Dhabi talks?
factCheck.description: No. The talks produced an agreement to arrange a prisoner exchange, but major territorial and security disagreements remain unresolved.
factCheck.content: The agreement to arrange a prisoner exchange is not a ceasefire or a peace agreement. Attacks continued after the talks, and the central territorial questions remain unresolved.
factCheck.verdict: False if presented as an end to the war.

factCheck.title: Fact Check: Has Kenya already been declared Ebola-free?
factCheck.description: No. Kenya has begun the 42-day countdown after the last patient was discharged. A declaration may be possible on 23 December if no new cases are recorded.
factCheck.content: The last patient has been discharged and the final contacts have completed monitoring. The formal countdown still has to be completed before the country can be declared free of the outbreak.
factCheck.verdict: Not yet. The countdown has begun.

factCheck.title: Fact Check: Does filing an appeal automatically suspend a court judgment in Nigeria?
factCheck.description: No. Filing an appeal does not automatically suspend the operation of a judgment. A stay of execution requires a separate court order.
factCheck.content: The distinction between an appeal, an application for a stay and an actual order granting a stay is important in reporting the ADC dispute. The legal position must be assessed from the relevant court documents and orders.

beyondStatement.title: Why Kenya's Ebola countdown still matters
beyondStatement.description: The discharge of the final patient is encouraging, but the 42-day surveillance period remains essential to confirming that transmission has stopped.
beyondStatement.content: Public-health success is not measured only by the last patient leaving hospital. Health authorities must continue surveillance, investigate alerts and support survivors. The countdown is designed to provide confidence that no further transmission has occurred.

beyondStatement.title: What a prisoner-exchange agreement does — and does not — mean
beyondStatement.description: An agreement to exchange prisoners can bring relief to families, but it does not resolve the political and military disagreements that sustain a war.
beyondStatement.content: A prisoner exchange is a humanitarian measure. Its implementation can build limited confidence between negotiating parties, but it does not establish a ceasefire, settle territorial disputes or guarantee a lasting peace.

leaders.implications: The handling of political disputes and electoral procedures will influence public confidence.
leaders.radiantWavesView: All political parties and public institutions should respect legal procedures and provide voters with clear information.

leaders.name: Atiku Abubakar
leaders.headline: Atiku's political plans remain affected by the ADC leadership dispute
leaders.report: The court dispute involving the ADC leadership has implications for the political plans of Atiku Abubakar and other opposition figures.
leaders.background: Atiku is a former vice-president and a prominent opposition politician.
leaders.implications: The legal outcome and the party's ability to establish a recognised leadership structure could influence opposition preparations for 2027.
leaders.radiantWavesView: Political supporters should follow verified court documents and official INEC statements rather than treat unresolved legal questions as settled facts.

leaders.name: Xi Jinping
leaders.headline: China and ASEAN continue negotiations over the South China Sea
leaders.report: China and ASEAN have missed their target for completing a code of conduct despite reported progress in negotiations.
leaders.background: China has overlapping maritime claims with several Southeast Asian countries.
leaders.implications: The negotiations affect maritime security, trade routes and regional relations.
leaders.radiantWavesView: A durable agreement will require clear rules, mutual respect and credible dispute-management mechanisms.

leaders.name: Cyril Ramaphosa
leaders.headline: African regional priorities include health security and political stability
leaders.report: Developments in East and Central Africa, including the Ebola response and South Sudan's election preparations, underline the importance of regional coordination.
leaders.background: South Africa remains an influential African state and an important participant in continental diplomacy.
leaders.implications: Regional cooperation is essential for managing cross-border health risks and political instability.
leaders.radiantWavesView: African governments and regional institutions need sustained cooperation, transparent information and practical support.

leaders.name: Marine Le Pen
leaders.headline: France's opposition landscape continues to take shape ahead of 2027
leaders.report: The emergence of potential candidates and debate around the post-Macron political landscape form part of a wider contest involving established opposition figures.
leaders.background: Marine Le Pen remains a prominent figure in French opposition politics.
leaders.implications: Candidate eligibility, alliances and the shape of the opposition field will be important factors in the 2027 contest.
leaders.radiantWavesView: French voters will need clear policy choices and credible candidates as the next presidential election approaches.

todaysBigQuestion.question: Can democratic institutions remain strong when political leaders and parties face pressure?
todaysBigQuestion.description: From the United States to Nigeria and Europe, public confidence depends on credible elections, independent institutions, accountability and respect for the rule of law. What should citizens expect from those who hold political power?

thoughtForToday.title: Truth is the foundation of public trust
thoughtForToday.quote: A well-informed society does not simply ask who is speaking; it asks what is known, what is proven and what still needs to be established.

radiantWavesPerspective.title: Beyond the headlines
radiantWavesPerspective.description: Today's developments show why responsible journalism must distinguish between an agreement and its implementation, a political announcement and a confirmed candidacy, and a legal application and an actual court order. RadiantWaves Media will continue to verify claims, provide context and explain the implications of events across Nigeria, Africa, Europe and the wider world.

sourcePolicy.title: Our Editorial Standards
sourcePolicy.description: RadiantWaves Media uses named sources and official statements to support its reporting. We distinguish verified facts from allegations, political claims, projections and opinions. Court proceedings are described according to the documents and orders confirmed at the time of publication. Our reports are independently written and contextualised.
principles: Use official statements and reputable news organisations as source material.
Provide context and explain why developments matter.
Correct errors when reliable new information becomes available.
